filename: An Improved Methodology to Estimate Cross-Scale Kinetic Energy Transfers from Third-Order Structure Functions using Regularized Least-Squares.pdf
title: An improved methodology to estimate cross-scale kinetic energy transfers from third-order structure functions using regularized least-squares
venue: Journal of Atmospheric and Oceanic Technology
code_availability: Python code for processing the GLAD and LASER drifter datasets, running the QG simulation, and estimating structure functions and spectral fluxes using regularized least-squares is available at https://github.com/manuelogtzv/SF3_RLS. PyQG model is available at https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.6380711. Arch 6.3.1 is available at https://zenodo.org/records/10981635.
testbed_rationale: The study develops an observational and diagnostic inverse methodology using regularized linear regression rather than establishing a machine learning parameterization benchmark dataset or testbed.
pain_points: Standard ordinary least squares overfits data and produces non-physical, highly oscillatory energy injection rates
Non-negative least squares (NNLS) cannot diagnose negative energy injections or energy sinks/convergence
Observational drifter data are sparse, non-uniformly sampled, and prone to clustering in convergence zones, generating highly non-Gaussian error distributions
Spatio-temporal correlation between drifter pair observations invalidates simple independent bootstrapping, requiring moving-block bootstrap techniques to avoid severe uncertainty underestimation
extraction_notes: The paper is supported by the NSF LEAP STC (#2019625). The mathematical technique employed is regularized least squares (ridge regression) to solve a discrete linear inverse problem formulated from third-order velocity structure functions.
